title: No orphan words: a line never ends alone on one word, and a before/after movement breaks into its two halves
body: Author's UX rule (2026-10-29), for every page and both locales. 1) The last line of a heading or paragraph never holds one word alone: v2.css and brief.css set text-wrap: balance on h1–h4 and short copy (.beat__body, .beat__label, .stage__wins li, .principle p) and text-wrap: pretty on running p/li. 2) No line ends on a dangling short word ('report: a' / 'choropleth'): the landing's beat titles and bodies go through glueShortWords (src/lib/highlight.ts), which ties every 1–2 letter word to the next with a no-break space. 3) A before/after metric is set as its two halves, one per line: 'de ~5 s' / 'a ~500 ms', never 'de ~5 s a' over a lone '~500 ms' (formatMetricLines in content/schema/format-metric.ts, .beat__line in v2.css). When adding copy or a new display surface, apply the same; check new text at 2560 px and on a phone, in Spanish and English (English wraps differently).
not_derivable: It is the author's design rule; the CSS shows the mechanism but not that it is a requirement to keep on every new piece of text.
